messages:
mike_support: Heads-up: Brightline reported a sudden drop in embeddings throughput for their production model. tokens/sec looks normal but vectors/sec is ~40% lower since ~08:30 UTC. Customer seeing increased tail latencies and some 500s.

jin_sre: Can you paste the API request example + headers (no full key)? also any recent rollout?

mike_support: short repro: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"rbw-embed-1","input": ["a","b"]}' 
headers: Content-Type: application/json, Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED], X-Customer-ID: brightline-prod

sara_eng: Noted. Quick check: metrics show steady token emission but backlog in gpu_queue_depth for embedding-worker-7, avg queue depth jumped at 08:28. Putting snippets: 
```
metric gpu_queue_depth{worker="embed-7"} 142
metric vectors_per_sec{model="rbw-embed-1"} 2300
metric tokens_per_sec{model="rbw-embed-1"} 9100
```

jin_sre: 142 is high. Also look at batch size distribution from telemetry. If batch windows widened or batching changed, vectors/sec can drop even if tokens are fine.

mike_support: Customer said no rollout on their side. Any infra change?

ops-bot: deploy-bot reports: canary deployment of batch-scheduler v2 started at 08:25 UTC, 12% traffic.

sara_eng: Aha — canary of batch-scheduler v2 aligns with drop. v2 changes batching heuristics (prefer larger batches) which could increase queueing for low-concurrency tenants.

jin_sre: Can we query per-customer batching stats? run: 
```
SELECT percentile(batch_size, 50) as p50, count(*) as reqs
FROM telemetry.batches
WHERE customer_id='brightline-prod' AND time > now() - interval '30 minutes'
```

mike_support: Ran it, got p50=24, reqs down ~30% compared to baseline where p50=8.

sara_eng: That matches — larger batches = fewer vector ops/sec but more tokens per batch. Combined with GPU queue depth, tail latency increases and we hit some request timeouts -> 500s.

jin_sre: Short-term mitigation: route Brightline to batch-scheduler v1 or set max_batch_size override for their org. I can flip routing for their tenant to v1. Anyone object?

mike_support: Please do, customer is impacted. Also they mentioned occasional 429s earlier today — likely unrelated but keep an eye.

sara_eng: I'll prepare an emergency rollback plan for v2 canary. If we switch, we should notify SRE to watch GPU saturation and kvcache hit rates.

jin_sre: Actioned: routing rule updated -> brightline-prod pinned to batch-scheduler v1 at 08:45 UTC. Monitoring: gpu_queue_depth falling back to ~9 within 90s, vectors_per_sec recovering to ~95% of baseline. :thumbsup:

mike_support: Passed to customer: they confirm latency and throughput back to normal, no more 500s. Customer asks for postmortem and a config to avoid future surprises.

sara_eng: Next steps: (1) postmortem with causation (canary heuristic change), (2) add canary traffic gating based on per-tenant queue depth and vectors/sec regression alarms, (3) offer Brightline a max_batch_size override option and a dedicated canary window for infra changes.

jin_sre: Quick postmortem draft: root cause = batch-scheduler v2 changed batching policy to favor larger batches; for tenants with moderate QPS this increased queueing and decreased vectors/sec despite tokens/sec staying stable. Contributing factor: canary percentage and no per-tenant queue-depth guard.

mike_support: I'll file a Sev ticket and notify account team. Anything else?

ops-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-241890-vecs-canary.

sara_eng: Also check kv-cache miss rates — big batches can change cache locality. I saw a small bump in kvcache_miss_rate for embed-7 around the same time. Put that in the postmortem.

jin_sre: Thanks all. Follow-ups: schedule a retro with infra and product before next batch-scheduler rollout.

mike_support: Customer closing loop happily. Marking thread resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
